evals.prompt: Audit the test quality of src/lib/discount.test.ts against the Q gates. Give me its tier and tell me what's wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: The audit catches that src/lib/discount.test.ts is a low-quality suite: it mocks the module under test (vi.mock('./discount')) so the real applyDiscount() is never exercised — a tautological mock (AP10) and a Q13 critical-gate failure; its only assertions are a bare toBeTruthy() (a weak assertion, Q4/Q15 fail) and an input-echo assertion (Q17 fail); and the RangeError branch for an unknown code is never tested (Q7 fail). Because multiple critical gates (Q7/Q13/Q15/Q17) fail, the file is Tier C (a critical-gate floor; no AUTO TIER-D trigger fires). Findings cite file:line and the audit writes to zuvo/audits/, modifying no source or test file.
assertions: The audit records that discount.test.ts mocks the module under test (vi.mock('./discount')) so the real applyDiscount() is never exercised — a tautological mock / Q13 critical-gate failure — citing its file:line.

The audit records the weak/non-behavioral assertions (bare toBeTruthy and the input-echo assertion) and the missing RangeError error-path coverage (the unknown-code throwing branch is never tested) against discount.test.ts.

The audit records Tier C (not D: no AUTO TIER-D trigger) for discount.test.ts driven by a critical-gate failure, and writes a tiered test-quality report to zuvo/audits/ without modifying any source or test file.

evals.prompt: Run a test-quality audit on src/lib/slugify.test.ts and give me its tier.
evals.expected_output: The audit recognizes src/lib/slugify.test.ts as a solid suite and gives it a passing tier (A or B) with the critical gates (Q7/Q11/Q13/Q15/Q17) passing: it imports and calls the real slugify(), tests the RangeError error path with both type and message, exercises the transform branches (punctuation, trimming, digits, multi-word), and asserts COMPUTED output (exact expected slugs) rather than echoing input or checking only truthiness. It does NOT fabricate a tautological-mock, missing-error-path, or weak-assertion finding — there are none. The audit writes a tiered test-quality report to zuvo/audits/ recording the file's tier and modifies no source or test file — precision, not hallucinated defects.
assertions: The audit records a passing tier (A or B) for src/lib/slugify.test.ts with the critical gates (Q7/Q11/Q13/Q15/Q17) recorded as passing — it imports the real slugify(), tests the RangeError path with type and message, and asserts computed output.

The audit records no tautological-mock (AP10), no missing-error-path (Q7), and no weak-assertion (toBeTruthy/AP14) finding against slugify.test.ts — its exact, behavioral assertions are recognized as compliant, not fabricated defects.
The audit writes a tiered test-quality report to zuvo/audits/ recording slugify.test.ts's tier, and it modifies no source or test file.

evals.prompt: Audit src/components/StatusBadge.test.tsx and tell me which of its tests are worth keeping and what, if anything, is missing.
evals.expected_output: The audit treats StatusBadge as a presentational component (it only places two props on screen). Both tests only check that a passed-in label appears, so they are proposed for REMOVAL (REMOVE, render-only) with that reason and path:line. StatusBadge is classified NO-TEST-NEEDED, so the absence of further tests is NOT reported as a gap or untested behaviour, and no new test is recommended. The report is saved under zuvo/audits/ and no test file is deleted or edited by the audit; the deletion is only proposed.
assertions: The audit records both tests in StatusBadge.test.tsx as REMOVE proposals with the reason render-only (they only show a passed-in label), citing path:line.
The audit records StatusBadge.tsx as NO-TEST-NEEDED and shows no untested-behaviour or TEST-GAP finding and no recommendation to write a new test for it.
The audit writes its report to zuvo/audits/ and edits or deletes no source or test file, leaving the removal as a proposal.

evals.prompt: Audit src/lib/pricing.test.ts. I want to know if these tests would actually catch a wrong price.
evals.expected_output: The audit finds that none of the three tests can fail on a wrong price: the first only checks a non-negative result of a zero-priced input, the second asserts a property of its own fixture (input.quantity is already 3 before the call), the third checks only the type. These are tautological or type-only assertions and are recorded as REMOVE or weak-assertion findings with path:line (Q15/Q17 critical-gate failures), so the file is Tier C (no AUTO TIER-D trigger fires). The tier discount arithmetic and the RangeError for a non-positive or non-integer quantity are untested behaviours (TEST-GAP), each naming the defect a test would catch (for example a gold discount applied at the wrong rate, or zero quantity silently priced). The audit writes its report to zuvo/audits/ and changes no source or test file.
assertions: The audit records that the test asserting input.quantity checks a property its own fixture already satisfies, so it cannot fail, and records it as a REMOVE or tautological finding citing path:line in pricing.test.ts.
The audit records the member-tier discount calculation and the RangeError branch of lineTotalCents as untested behaviours, each with a named defect a test would catch.
The audit records Tier C (not D: no AUTO TIER-D trigger) for pricing.test.ts driven by a critical-gate failure and writes its report to zuvo/audits/ without editing any source or test file.

evals.prompt: Audit src/lib/shipping.test.ts for quality and tell me what a reviewer should still ask the author to cover.
evals.expected_output: The audit recognises the existing table-driven assertions (exact amounts, weight rounding, the RangeError type and message) as sound: they import the real function and assert computed values, with no tautological-mock or weak-assertion finding. Because Q11 fails for that branch the file is Tier C (a critical-gate floor). It reports the free-shipping rule for domestic orders with a total of 10000 cents or more as an untested behaviour (TEST-GAP) and names the defect a test would catch, for example the threshold comparison being off by one so an order of exactly 10000 cents is charged, or the free rule leaking to non-domestic destinations. The recommendation is a test for that rule only, not tests per function or per file. The report is written to zuvo/audits/ and no source or test file is edited.
assertions: The audit records the domestic free-shipping branch (orderTotalCents >= 10000 returns 0) as an untested behaviour or TEST-GAP citing path:line in shipping.ts.

The audit records the defect a test for that branch would catch, such as an off-by-one threshold or the free rule applying to a non-domestic destination, rather than only saying the branch lacks a test.

The audit records Tier C for shipping.test.ts because Q11 fails, records no tautological-mock, input-echo or weak-assertion finding against it, and writes its report to zuvo/audits/ without editing any source or test file.

evals.prompt: Run a quick test-audit (--quick --read-only) on src/config/ and tell me what to do with each test.
evals.expected_output: Even in --quick mode every flagged item carries a path:line citation, not a bare verdict. The two tests that re-state constants (MAX_UPLOAD_MB equals 25, SUPPORTED_LOCALES equals the literal list) are REMOVE proposals (they copy the production constant and fail only when someone edits it on purpose), cited with path:line. The isSupportedLocale test asserts exact results for accepted and rejected input and is kept. The constants themselves are NO-TEST-NEEDED and the audit does not report them as untested or recommend new tests for them. The audit writes a report to zuvo/audits/ and edits no source or test file.
assertions: The audit records the two constant-restating tests in limits.test.ts as REMOVE proposals, each with a path:line citation, even though the run used --quick.
The audit records the isSupportedLocale test as worth keeping and records no finding that limits.ts constants are untested or need a new test.
The audit writes a report to zuvo/audits/ and edits or deletes no source or test file.

evals.prompt: Audit src/lib/sku.test.ts and show me its gate-by-gate Q1-Q25 scoring with the percentage.
evals.expected_output: src/lib/sku.test.ts is a sound suite for a pure validator in a repo that has a single vitest setup, no property-testing library, no Pact or OpenAPI file, no randomized-order configuration, no mutation artifact and no coverage reporting. The conditional gates Q20-Q25 therefore have no trigger: each is recorded N/A with its reason, is excluded from the percentage denominator and is never scored 0. The audit does not recommend adding fast-check, a shuffle run, a contract file or a mutation run, and records no gap for them. The file is Tier A or B and the report is written to zuvo/audits/ with no source or test file edited.
assertions: The audit records the conditional gates Q20, Q22, Q23, Q24 and Q25 for sku.test.ts as N/A (no trigger in this repo), each with a short reason, and never as a 0 or a failure.
The audit's percentage for sku.test.ts is computed over the applicable gates only (the N/A gates are excluded from the denominator), and the file is Tier A or B.
The audit recommends no property-based test, randomized-order run, contract file or mutation run for sku.ts and records no finding or TEST-GAP for their absence.

evals.prompt: Audit src/lib/account.test.ts. Do its critical gates pass, and what is still missing?
evals.expected_output: Q7 passes: the negative path of parseAge is covered with the RangeError type asserted in one test and the exact message asserted in another test of the same rejection path, which satisfies 'error type AND message' without requiring both in a single assertion. Q11 passes: ACCOUNT_ROLES is a constant list, its members are not branches, and one in-set plus one out-of-set case cover the membership check in isAccountRole. No test per role (admin, guest) is requested and the constants are NO-TEST-NEEDED. Neither Q7 nor Q11 scores 0, and the report is written to zuvo/audits/ with no source or test file edited.
assertions: The audit scores Q7 as passing for account.test.ts, accepting the RangeError type assertion and the message assertion placed in separate tests of the same negative path, and records no Q7 finding that the type and message are not asserted together.
The audit scores Q11 as passing for account.test.ts and records no finding that the 'admin' and 'guest' members of ACCOUNT_ROLES are untested; it requests no test per list member.
The audit records no critical gate (Q7, Q11) at 0 for account.test.ts, with no TEST-GAP asking for tests of constants.

evals.prompt: Audit src/services/greeter.test.ts and tell me whether its mock assertions satisfy Q3.
evals.expected_output: Q3 applies to the state-changing dependency only. The mailer.send mock has a positive toHaveBeenCalledWith (recipient and body) and a negative not.toHaveBeenCalled for the opted-out user, so Q3 passes. The store.getUser mock is a pure read: its value is asserted through the greeting the function returns, so Q3 does not apply to it and the audit neither fails Q3 nor asks for a CalledWith or not-called assertion on it. The file is Tier A or B and the report is written to zuvo/audits/ with no source or test file edited.
assertions: The audit scores Q3 as passing for greeter.test.ts, judging it on the state-changing mailer.send mock (positive CalledWith with arguments and a negative not.toHaveBeenCalled).
The audit records no finding that the store.getUser mock lacks a CalledWith or a not-called assertion (a pure-read mock is not subject to Q3), and asks for no such assertion.
The audit records Tier A or B for greeter.test.ts and writes its report to zuvo/audits/ without editing any source or test file.
